summary: Step 2 of 3 after sign-up. The player picks every way they like to explore (9 options, pick any number). Continue shows what their picks unlocked; Skip shows a plain default Explore. Picks tune what they see first.

rows.then: No options picked. Continue is disabled and reads “Pick one or more to continue”.
It turns on and joins the picks, in the order tapped. Continue shows the count (“Continue 3”).
It turns off and leaves the picks. At zero picks, Continue is disabled again.
Saves the picks and opens What your picks unlocked.
Saves no picks and opens the default Explore.

rows.when: Swipe a card right past 80px, or tap ✓ Yes
rows.then: Picks that option and shows the next card.

rows.when: Swipe left past 80px, or tap ✕ Not for me
rows.then: Skips that option and shows the next card.
The card springs back. Nothing is picked.
“That's the whole deck” with Go through again, which restarts at card 1 and keeps the picks.

rows.when: Tap ✕ on a chip under Your yeses

rows.then: One card per pick, in the order picked: icon, what it unlocks, one line about it.

Ends the first-time flow and opens Explore, tuned to the picks.
Back to the pick screen with every pick still on.

edgeCases: All nine picked: nine unlock cards, the list scrolls, Start exploring stays pinned at the bottom.
Bookerton chat (F): at 6 or more picks he says “You like a bit of everything”; unpicking says “No problem, crossed that one off”.
Reduced motion on: no flying cards, pulses or typing dots; states change instantly.
No line ends with one word alone, on any screen size.
Option ids are fixed (stories, gems, steps, fog, daily, together, city, treadmill, puzzles); labels can change without breaking analytics.
